unusual_experiment.name: SHARED_EXPORTER_TORN_TOBYTES_SNAPSHOT
unusual_experiment.environment: isolated ChatGPT container; NOT Vercel Sandbox
unusual_experiment.setup: 32 MiB multiprocessing.shared_memory buffer; independent writer process repeatedly alternated the whole producer buffer between byte values 0x11 and 0xEE while the reader admitted a contiguous one-byte memoryview and called tobytes().
unusual_experiment.counterhypothesis: An owned copy produced by memoryview.tobytes() is not by itself a producer-epoch-consistent snapshot when the underlying exporter can be mutated concurrently outside the copying process.
unusual_experiment.what_this_refutes: The broad inference that contiguous bytes-like memoryview + copy automatically yields provenance-stable Clay Bytes for shared or externally mutable exporters.
unusual_experiment.what_this_does_not_refute: A copy performed while an enforceable exclusive lease/epoch is held, or immutable built-in bytes backing, may still be valid. This experiment does not establish general semantics for every bytearray or exporter implementation.

ordinary_followup_control.candidate_fence: Reject memoryview exporters outside an explicitly admitted ownership set before copying; unknown/shared mmap-backed exporters fail closed as BYTES_VIEW_EXPORTER_UNLEASED.

retain: Clay Bytes must represent owned immutable bytes after admission.
Unknown/shared borrowed exporters cannot be promoted merely because a copy operation is requested.
A separate mutable/shared Buffer contract needs explicit ownership/lease/epoch semantics before zero-copy or snapshot claims are accepted.
architecture_collapse.preferred_safe_direction: Keep canonical Bytes fail-closed for shared/unknown mutable exporters; introduce Buffer/lease/epoch semantics separately rather than hiding concurrency authority inside host memoryview behavior.
architecture_collapse.strongest_remaining_counter_reality: Direct bytearray or memoryview(bytearray) copying may be safe under a restricted single-owner contract, but the current Clay boundary does not encode or prove that ownership contract.
